headline: GOLD CRESTS $4,100 AS FED HOLDS AT 3.5% — $155 Recovery From July's $3,975 Low In Single US Session
snippet: Gold futures pushed to $4,130 per ounce in early US trading on July 30 — the first time the metal has traded convincingly above $4,100 since June — after the Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate steady at 3.50–3.75% on July 29. The $155 single-session recovery from the July 14 intraday low of $3,975 is one of the sharpest short-covering rallies of 2026 and confirms that the $4,000 level is now functioning as a structural floor rather than resistance. Earlier in the day, gold was trading near $4,030 in Asian markets following mild post-FOMC selling; the US open brought fresh institutional buying that pushed it decisively above the psychologically important $4,100 threshold.

headline: COPPER +2.1% TO $6.44/LB: FED PAUSE FUELS RALLY AS CHILE WINTER STORM KNOCKED OUT 1.6M TONNES OF ANNUAL OUTPUT
snippet: Copper surged 2.1% to $6.44 per pound on July 30 — the metal's largest single-day gain in six weeks — as the Federal Reserve's rate hold removed the near-term demand headwind, while supply constraints from Chile's July winter storm continue to ripple through the market. Severe storms across northern Chile between July 14 and 20 forced Codelco, Anglo American, Antofagasta, and Lundin Mining to suspend or curtail operations at mines collectively representing approximately 1.6 million tonnes of annual production capacity. Lundin's Caserones operation in the Atacama region lost grid power on July 18 with two transmission towers confirmed damaged; full output there depends on rebuilt transmission infrastructure. The convergence of a macro tailwind (Fed hold) and a structural supply crunch (Chile) has reaccelerated the 2026 copper bull thesis for retail investors positioned in copper-focused junior developers.

headline: GALLEON GOLD ZONE 9: 16.84 g/t AU CORE INSIDE 6.8 g/t OVER 19.45m — West Cache Extends to 500m Vertical Depth in Timmins Abitibi (TSXV: GGO)
snippet: Galleon Gold Corp. (TSXV: GGO) reported July 30 that drill hole WC-26-241 at the West Cache Gold Project intersected 6.8 g/t gold over 19.45 metres — including a high-grade core of 16.84 g/t Au over 6.15 metres — within a broader envelope of 4.72 g/t Au over 29.05 metres, confirming the high-grade spine of Zone #9 at depth. The project is located 13 km west of Timmins, Ontario, along Provincial Highway 101 in the Western Porcupine Gold Camp on the Destor-Porcupine Fault Zone — the same structural corridor that hosts the Porcupine camp's historical multi-million-ounce deposits. Separate drilling has now extended the Zone #9 corridor to over 500 metres of vertical extent, well beyond the originally modelled resource envelope, suggesting meaningful resource growth potential ahead of an updated estimate.

headline: WHY SILVER CAN'T BREAK $60 EVEN WITH A FED HOLD — The Structural Deficit vs. the Market's Reality
snippet: Silver opened at $57.97 per ounce on July 30 — down 0.2% from Wednesday's close — and remained below the $60 resistance level despite the Federal Reserve's rate hold, a level it has failed to decisively clear since late April. The divergence from gold (which recovered to $4,100) underscores silver's dual nature as both a monetary metal and an industrial commodity: while PCE inflation data and FOMC decisions move gold directly, silver's $60 ceiling reflects uncertainty about near-term industrial demand in a slowing global manufacturing cycle. The dynamic is analytically significant — the six-consecutive-year structural supply deficit (46.3 million ounces projected for 2026) provides the fundamental floor, but macro timing has repeatedly deferred the ratio compression trade. Silver at $58 with gold at $4,100 implies a gold-silver ratio of approximately 71:1, historically extreme and a setup retail investors should understand before the next catalyst closes the gap.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY OFF 50% FROM PEAK: MOTLEY FOOL MAPS THE REALISTIC 10-YEAR BULL CASE FOR THE BATTERED STOCK (NYSE: UEC)
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE: UEC) shares have fallen approximately 50% from their early 2026 peak as uranium spot prices, which surged to $86+ per pound, have consolidated and pulled back through the year. In a July 30 analysis, Motley Fool makes the case that the valuation reset is creating a multi-year entry point: Uranium Energy held 1.46 million pounds of physical uranium as of its Q3 2026 quarter-end, operates multiple low-cost ISR production platforms in Texas and Wyoming, and is positioned to benefit from structurally growing demand — AI data centers, government SMR commitments, and reactor restarts across Europe and Japan. The piece acknowledges the near-term headwinds (oversupply fears, contract pricing lag) but argues the decade-long supply gap between reactor demand and mine output makes current prices a buying opportunity for patient investors willing to hold through the consolidation phase.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS ESTABLISHES FOOTHILLS DISTRICT: UP TO 44.5% TREO AT SURFACE — Heavy REE Push Expands Beyond Shiloh in Georgia (NYSE: REA)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Rare Earths Americas
snippet: Rare Earths Americas Inc. (NYSE American: REA) announced on July 29 the formal establishment of the Foothills Rare Earths District, expanding its Georgia exploration footprint well beyond the company's initial Shiloh discovery to encompass multiple high-priority target areas. Surface samples across the Newbill and Pipeline properties returned grades up to 44.5% total rare earth oxides (TREO), with 13 samples ranging between 17% and 44.5% — exceptional surface grades for a sediment-hosted rare earth system. The deposit is enriched in heavy rare earth elements including dysprosium and terbium, the two most strategically critical inputs for permanent magnets in EV motors and defence applications. With China now blacklisting European defence companies from rare earth supply, REA's Georgia project — on private land, in a streamlined permitting jurisdiction — represents exactly the kind of domestic heavy rare earth asset Washington has been spending billions trying to develop.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: 2 RARE EARTH STOCKS TO BUY RIGHT NOW — And One to Sell As the Supply Chain War Redraws the Sector
snippet: Motley Fool's July 29 rare earth sector analysis lays out a buy/sell framework at a time when US rare earth equities have collectively surged 81% in the first half of 2026 and China's export controls on dysprosium, terbium, and permanent magnets have shifted the sector from speculative to strategic. The article identifies USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) as the two companies best positioned to capture near-term government contract flow and offtake demand from EV and defence manufacturers, while flagging a third name whose current valuation has run well past its development timeline and operational reality. For retail investors navigating a sector that is simultaneously speculative and geopolitically essential, this kind of buy/sell differentiation is more useful than broad sector bullishness.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS: CHINA BOUGHT 48 TONNES GOLD IN MAY ALONE — Real Accumulation Running 5x Official PBoC Reports; $4,900 Year-End Target Intact
snippet: A Goldman Sachs research note, highlighted by Money Metals Exchange and published on GoldSeek on July 28, estimates that China's People's Bank of China acquired more than 48 tonnes of gold through London's over-the-counter market in May 2026 — the largest monthly purchase in over a year and nearly five times the 10 tonnes officially reported in PBoC disclosures for the same period. Applying a conservative 2x multiplier to full-year 2026 data, Goldman estimates China has accumulated 80+ tonnes so far this year; using the May ratio, the real figure could be nearly 200 tonnes. The bank frames the hidden accumulation as a multi-decade reserve diversification away from dollar assets and explicitly cites it as the structural price floor supporting its $4,900 per troy ounce end-2026 gold forecast — a figure that looks achievable if China continues buying at the May pace through year-end regardless of Federal Reserve policy.

headline: T2 METALS BREAKS 15-YEAR SILENCE AT AURORA GOLD-SILVER — First Drill in Yukon's Tombstone Gold Belt Targets Au-Cu-Sb System (TSXV: TWO)
snippet: T2 Metals Corp. (TSXV: TWO) announced July 30 that drilling has commenced at the Aurora Gold-Silver Project in the Yukon's Tombstone Gold Belt — the company's first drill program in the Yukon and the first drilling at Aurora in over 15 years. The 2026 program follows a successful early summer mapping and prospecting campaign that identified new zones of gold, copper, and antimony mineralization, a multi-metal association characteristic of the orogenic gold systems that host the Tombstone Belt's best deposits. The Aurora project sits in the same belt as the Coffee Gold Project (Yukon Goldfields) and the Lone Star discoveries. With no drill results yet, this is a watch-list item: in $4,100 gold markets, the first hole at a historically undrilled prospect in a proven gold belt is the kind of catalyst that can re-rate small-cap explorers rapidly. First assays are expected in Q3 2026.
